Riverside Library Network: Annual Review 2025

Overview
In 2025 the Riverside Library Network served 412,000 visitors across its 9 branches, up from 368,000 in 2024. The increase came mostly from the two branches that extended their opening hours to 9 pm on weekdays in March. Digital loans grew faster than physical ones: e-book and audiobook loans reached 156,000, a rise of 22%, while physical loans stayed flat at about 610,000.

Budget
The network's operating budget was $7.4 million, of which 58% went to staff and 19% to the collection. A one-off grant of $350,000 from the city paid for new self-service kiosks in 5 branches. Energy costs fell by 11% after the heating system in the central library was replaced in January.

Programmes
The homework club ran in all branches and had 2,300 registered children. The digital skills course for adults was fully booked: 640 people completed it, and the waiting list closed at 210 names. The mobile library van visited 14 villages every two weeks but missed 23 scheduled stops because of breakdowns.

Challenges and next steps
Staff turnover remained high at 17%, and two branch manager posts were vacant for more than six months. The board approved a plan to repair or replace the mobile van in 2026, to open a tenth branch in the Northgate district by the end of 2026, and to test Sunday opening at the central library from April 2026. The review recommends tracking the use of the new kiosks before buying more.

Load test report: checkout service v3.2

We ran the checkout service on 4 instances (8 vCPU, 16 GB each) behind the existing load balancer and replayed 30 minutes of production traffic at 1x, 2x and 3x volume.

At 1x the median latency was 84 ms and the p99 was 410 ms. At 2x the p99 rose to 690 ms but stayed under the 800 ms objective. At 3x the error rate climbed to 2.7% after 11 minutes because the database connection pool (max 50 per instance) was exhausted; latency then exceeded 3 seconds for 6% of requests.

Raising the pool to 80 connections and adding a read replica removed the errors in a second 3x run, with a p99 of 720 ms. CPU never went above 65% on any instance, so the bottleneck is the database, not the service. We recommend shipping the pool change with v3.2 and planning the read replica before the holiday peak.

Compte rendu du conseil municipal du 14 octobre 2026

Le conseil a adopté le budget rectifié de la piscine municipale. Les travaux de rénovation coûteront 1,2 million d'euros, dont 400 000 euros financés par la région. La piscine fermera du 1er décembre au 31 mars.

Le projet de piste cyclable entre la gare et le lycée a été reporté : deux propriétaires contestent le tracé. Une réunion publique aura lieu en novembre.

Enfin, le conseil a voté à l'unanimité la gratuité de la cantine pour les familles aux revenus les plus modestes, à partir de janvier.

The new parental leave policy starts on 1 January 2027. Every employee with at least six months of service can take 16 weeks of paid leave after a birth or adoption, regardless of gender. Pay during the leave is 100% of base salary for the first 10 weeks and 60% for the remaining 6 weeks.

Employees must tell their manager at least 8 weeks before the leave starts. The leave can be split into two blocks within the first year. Employees on fixed-term contracts are covered if their contract runs past the end of the leave.

Questions go to the People team. Managers will get a short training session in December on handling leave requests and covering workloads.

Incident report IR-2026-031 (confidential)

On 9 October 2026 at 02:14 an attacker used a stolen VPN password belonging to a contractor to log in to the internal network. Over 3 hours the attacker copied a database export containing the names, email addresses and hashed passwords of 18,400 customers. No payment card data was stored in that export.

The intrusion was detected at 05:20 when the data transfer triggered an alert. The contractor account was disabled at 05:31 and all VPN passwords were reset the same day. Multi-factor authentication for the VPN, planned for 2027, was switched on for all accounts on 11 October.

Customers were notified by email on 12 October and the data protection authority on 11 October, within the 72-hour deadline.

Company update for the sales team. The new pricing page went live this week and early feedback has been positive. Informe de la biblioteca escolar, curso 2025-2026

Durante el curso se prestaron 3.240 libros, un 15 % más que el año anterior. El club de lectura de los jueves tuvo 28 alumnos inscritos. La biblioteca recibió 600 libros nuevos gracias a una donación de la asociación de familias.

El principal problema es el espacio: en las horas de recreo no hay sitio para todos. El equipo propone abrir también por la tarde dos días a la semana a partir de enero.
